title: Linux process exit codes and signals
summary: Distinguish normal exit status from signal termination without treating one number as a root cause.

concepts.title: Exit status
concepts.explanation: A process can return a numeric status when it finishes. The value is evidence about the termination path, not a complete diagnosis.

concepts.title: Signal termination
concepts.explanation: A shell may report 128 plus a signal number, but runtimes and wrappers can present termination differently.

concepts.title: Context matters
concepts.explanation: Container, systemd, Kubernetes and shell layers can preserve or transform exit evidence.

limitations: An exit code alone does not identify the failing line, configuration, dependency or safe fix.
Signal-derived values should be confirmed with the originating runtime or service manager.
